cases.statement: One person: a 5-year-old girl from consanguineous parents (northeast Iran) with periodic fever from age 2 and episodic oral ulcers, eye redness/eyelid swelling, abdominal pain, diarrhea, perianal swelling and dysuria; found by WES. Zygosity is not stated explicitly for this variant.

people.label: patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: not reported for this variant (the paper only states in general that the disease is caused by heterozygous variants)
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); additional variants in PIK3R1, HBB, SERPINA1 and VPS37A reported
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent periodic fever from age 2 (every 20 days, ~3 days); oral aphthous ulcers; eye redness/pain and eyelid swelling; abdominal pain and diarrhea; perianal swelling and dysuria

quotes.quote: A five-year-old Caucasian consanguine girl presented to our clinic with a history of recurrent periodic fever from the age of second year.
Each febrile episode occurred every 20 days and lasted approximately three days.

During these episodes, she experienced redness and pain in the eyes, swelling of the upper and lower eyelids, abdominal pain, oral aphthous ulcers, diarrhea, perianal tenderness and swelling, and dysuria.
During early infancy, the patient had a brief febrile convulsive seizure, following neurological workup.
Following initiation of infliximab, the patient exhibited a marked clinical improvement, and only one self-limited febrile episode over an eight-month follow-up period.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Features overlap the paper's description of the disease (fever, oral ulcers, GI symptoms, eye involvement). MEFV testing (12 common variants) was negative, IBD findings were absent on GI evaluation, ANA negative. WES found additional variants in other genes that the authors regard as possible modifiers, not the primary cause. Perianal swelling, dysuria and infant seizure are described by the authors as less typical.

quotes.quote: The patient was also tested for familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) 12 common MEFV gene variant alleles, which returned negative, helping to rule out this common autoinflammatory differential diagnosis.
Gastrointestinal evaluation did not reveal findings suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
Additional variants were detected in PIK3R1, HBB, and SERPINA1, which were considered to play a potential modifier role but were not thought to be the primary cause of her symptoms.
One difference in our case is the presence of perianal swelling resembling hemorrhoidal inflammation and dysuria, which are less commonly emphasized in the published HA20 literatures.

de_novo.statement: Parents were not tested; Sanger confirmation in the patient and parents was planned but not done. Seizure family history is stated negative; no other family history reported.

quotes.quote: the patient had seizures in infancy with negative family history of seizure and phenobarbital therapy
We planned to confirm these variants in the patient and parents by Sanger sequencing, but some unpredictable limitations delayed that.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion predicted to cause a frameshift, p.(Asp253GlufsTer9), from the batch HGVS; the paper writes p. Asp253fs. The paper states the disease mechanism as heterozygous loss of function / haploinsufficiency (general, not tested for this variant).

quotes.quote: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a recently recognized monogenic autoinflammatory and immune-dysregulation syndrome caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene, which encodes the ubiquitin-editing protein A20.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a likely pathogenic variant (abstract and case section), but also 'a pathogenic variant' (introduction) and 'probable pathogenic variants' (discussion). No ACMG criteria given.

quotes.quote: The analysis identified a likely pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3 (TNFAIP3 Chr6 138197257 138197257 C: NM_001270507.2: (5/9): c.759delC: p. Asp253fs), consistent with a diagnosis of Behçet-like autoinflammatory syndrome (HA20).
WES revealed a pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3 with additional variants in PIK3R1, HBB, and SERPINA1 possibly modifying the phenotype.
From the genetic perspective, this patient was found to carry probable pathogenic variants in TNFAIP3 (among others).

concerns: Transcript in the paper is NM_001270507.2, not the batch transcript NM_001270508.2; the c.759 position and protein agree per the batch protein_check, but the panel may wish to confirm the numbering is identical on both transcripts.
Genomic coordinate given on GRCh37 as 'Chr6 138197257 138197257 C' (no explicit deletion notation).
Zygosity of the variant is not stated for the patient.
WES-only finding: no Sanger confirmation and no parental testing.

Other variants in the same person: PIK3R1, HBB, SERPINA1 (authors: possible modifiers) and one in VPS37A, which the authors report separately with their own label (case section); specific variants not given.
The paper's own wording of the authors' classification is inconsistent across sections (see authors_classification).
notes_for_panel: Single case report with WES (GATK, GRCh37). Treatment response to infliximab is reported. The infant febrile seizure is described by the authors as possibly coincidental.
